title: Dedicated capacity weekly prep - 1:1 + forecasting
body:
Purpose: prep notes for weekly dedicated capacity sync and upcoming 1:1 with Maya. Focus: GPU pool forecast for next quarter, reservation sizing, autoscaling policy tweaks, and open action items.

Agenda draft:
- Quick status (5m): current pool utilization, major incidents last week
- Forecast (15m): demand signals, sticky customers, expected growth by product area
- Reservations & commits (10m): which tenants need reserved nodes; evaluate over/under-provisioning
- Autoscaling policy (15m): evaluate min/max, cooldowns, scale step sizes, burst capacity cadence
- Risk & mitigation (10m): capacity shortfall scenarios and fallbacks (model variants, routing)
- Actions & owners (5m)

Key metrics (current snapshot as of 2026-03-02):
- Total reserved GPUs: 420 (p4d-equivalent) across 12 pools
- Avg steady utilization (last 7d): 62%
- Peak utilization last 7d: 89% (2026-02-26 14:10 UTC - product A rollout)
- Autoscaled transient usage: added 48 GPUs across pools during peak bursts
- Cost per reserved GPU (monthly): $5,800 est (includes infra and infra-ops amortization)

Forecast assumptions for Q2 planning:
- Product A: expected +35% q/q inference traffic due to new feature rollout (on track for mid-April)
- Product B: stable +5% q/q; will require more low-latency reserved capacity for enterprise customers
- New enterprise RFPs: probability weighted additional +60 GPUs starting May if we win 2 of 3 prospective deals
- Model migrations: plan to roll Model-X (fp16) -> Model-X-q4 (8-bit quant) for cost savings in late May (reduces GPU time per request by ~18%)

Preliminary capacity ask (Q2 May-Jun):
- Baseline (keep current): 420 GPUs
- Conservative add: +30 GPUs reserved (to 450) to reduce sustained autoscaling churn for Product A ramp
- Aggressive add: +80 GPUs reserved (to 500) if enterprise commitments finalize (action: commit threshold = 40% customer acceptance by 2026-04-15)

Autoscaling policy notes / proposed tweaks:
- Current policy: scale step = 8 GPUs, cooldown = 6m, min idle buffer = 10% of pool size
- Problem: frequent small spikes cause repeated scale-outs -> high provisioning churn and e2e latency jumps during provisioning windows
- Proposal:
  - increase scale step to 16 GPUs for pools >64 GPUs (reduce frequent smaller scale ops)
  - introduce dynamic cooldown: base 6m + additional 2m per scale in last 30m
  - set minimum idle buffer to 12% for Product A pools during rollout windows
  - pre-warm policy: schedule predictable pre-warm (burst) windows for week-of-release (configurable via rollout tags)

Risk scenarios & fallbacks:
- If reserved capacity < demand during Product A ramp:
  - fallback to Model-X-q4 variant when available (latency impact +6-8ms, cost -18%)
  - route low-priority homogenous batch workloads to cheaper shared pools (action: implement route policy by 2026-04-01)
  - temporary uplift of burst capacity via cloud spot pools (ops playbook required)

Open questions to discuss with Maya:
- Threshold for converting autoscaled GPUs to reserved (TLDR: at what sustained utilization and revenue confidence do we commit?)
- Tolerance for increased buffer (12% vs 10%) - tradeoff: cost vs rollout risk
- Buy-in for pre-warm/runbook automation for coordinated releases

Action items (owner, due):
- Jordan: run revised cost model with proposed reserved +30 and +80 scenarios; include pf of quant migration savings (due 2026-03-06)
- Maya: confirm enterprise RFP timelines and hard-commit thresholds from sales (due 2026-03-05)
- Alex M: prototype dynamic cooldown changes in staging autoscaler (PR + perf run, due 2026-03-12)
- Priya: add routing rule to low-priority batches to shared pools and draft playbook for spot uplifts (due 2026-03-19)
- Ops: update on-call runbook for capacity shortfall incidents to include Model variant fallback steps (ops ticket: ENG-4890)

Notes to self:
- Bring the 30/80 numbers as scenarios rather than recommendations - want alignment from Maya on risk appetite
- Pull last 90-day per-tenant billing to match utilization trends (ticket: FIN-1212)
- Follow up with infra-procurement re: lead time for reserved GPU orders (typical ~6-8 weeks)

Relevant links / refs:
- Forecast sheet: https://sheets.redwood/internal/dedicated-forecast-q2
- Autoscaler runbook: confluence.redwood/internal/dedicated-autoscaler
- Recent incident notes: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01234/p1676991234000

Meeting prep checklist:
- Share agenda + metrics snapshot with Maya and Alex 24h before sync (Jordan)
- Attach forecast sheet and cost model to meeting invite (Jordan)
- Bring short script for how pre-warm tags will be applied during release windows (Alex)

Quick TL;DR for 1:1:
- We probably need a small reserved bump (+30) to smooth the Product A rollout unless sales confirms enterprise commitments by mid-April. Autoscaler tuning (larger steps + dynamic cooldown) should reduce churn; pre-warm for release windows is high ROI. Need Maya sign-off on risk tolerance and procurement timelines.

End of notes.
